documents.body:

events.reason: Severe right eye pain and blurred vision

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department record, visit 2024-05-09.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal AF on warfarin, systolic heart failure, Parkinson's disease, and past amiodarone lung toxicity, thyrotoxicosis and digoxin toxicity, arriving with four hours of sudden, severe pain in the right eye and blurred vision, with nausea and vomiting.
Medications per patient: benztropine; also warfarin, metoprolol succinate, digoxin, furosemide (outside list also shows amiodarone 200 mg). Allergy: sulfa drugs (rash).

Exam: right eye red with conjunctival injection, cornea hazy, pupil mid-dilated and unreactive to light, visual acuity reduced on the right. Intraocular pressure 48 mmHg right, 14 mmHg left. Fundus poorly seen through the corneal edema.

Impression: acute angle-closure glaucoma, right eye.
ED course: timolol, apraclonidine and pilocarpine drops to the right eye; IV mannitol. Acetazolamide held because of the sulfa allergy. Antiemetic given. Ophthalmology saw her in the department and will perform laser iridotomy in the morning. Discharged to ophthalmology follow-up.

medications.sig: Instill 1 drop in the right eye 4 times daily for 1 week

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology. Visits 2024-05-10, 2024-05-11 and 2024-05-24.

Seen from the ED with acute angle closure of the right eye. Laser peripheral iridotomy right eye on 5/10, uncomplicated. Next day the right IOP was 15 mmHg and the cornea had cleared. Prednisolone acetate 1% four times a day to the right eye for one week. On 5/24 a prophylactic laser iridotomy was done on the left eye, which had a narrow angle; both iridotomies are open.

Her benztropine may be continued now that both iridotomies are patent. She has a visually significant cataract in the right eye and we have discussed lens surgery this summer as the definitive step.
Allergy: sulfa (rash).

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for eye

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the ED for acute angle closure on the right, treated with drops and mannitol, then laser iridotomy by ophthalmology on 5/10. Eye now comfortable, vision improving, on steroid drops for the week. Left-eye laser planned 5/24. Asked whether her Parkinson's pill caused it: benztropine can narrow the angle, and ophthalmology will say whether it can continue once both eyes are lasered.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Right eye mildly injected, pupil reactive. Heart regular, lungs clear.
Plan: INR today (warfarin through all this). Await ophthalmology letter. Missed April visit covered today.

reports.text: Bilateral screening views. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. No change from 2022.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Your screening mammogram is normal. Letter to follow in the mail.

documents.title: Ophthalmic Surgery Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmic surgery center, 2024-08-06.

Procedure: phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens, right eye. Indication: visually significant cataract after acute angle closure, treated with iridotomy in May. Topical and intracameral anesthesia. Warfarin continued (clear-corneal approach). No complications. Postoperative day 1 IOP normal, lens centered. Usual drops for 4 weeks. Allergy: sulfa (rash).

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Had right cataract surgery 8/6; seeing much better out of that eye, colors brighter. No eye pain. Otherwise well; summer was good.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Right eye quiet. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
Plan: BMP, digoxin, INR. Cataract surgery added to surgical history. Flu/COVID at a nurse visit in October.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Left voicemail: INR fine, keep the same warfarin dose, next check in 4-5 weeks.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza (left arm) and 2024-25 COVID (right arm) given, VIS provided. INR drawn. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, age 72 last week.

This year: angle closure of the right eye in May (iridotomies both eyes), right cataract lens in August. Nothing cardiac. Neurology letter due.
Function: independent. One stumble on the porch step, no fall. Vision better since surgery.
PHQ-2: 1 (a few low days in the dark afternoons).
Meds unchanged: metoprolol succinate 50, digoxin 0.125, furosemide 40, warfarin 5 per INR, benztropine 1 BID. Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema.
Plan: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, Mg, INR. Tdap given (last one she cannot recall). Mammogram again in 2026 if she wishes. Colonoscopy due 2028; we will revisit at 75.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, visit 2024-12-02.

Stable year from a heart standpoint; eye problems noted. Brief palpitations now and then, no syncope. Sinus rhythm today. Weight steady, no orthopnea beyond baseline.
Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg, digoxin 0.125 mg, furosemide 40 mg, warfarin, benztropine. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Plan: no change. Yearly follow-up.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR within 2-3. No bleeding. Continue 5 mg daily.
